ownership.insiderDesc: Two-founder structure with beneficiary certificates (beneficiary certificates, carrying no economic rights, only additional voting rights): Daniel Ek (founder, Executive Chairman since 1 January 2026, ~14,3% of the capital / ~29,1% of the voting rights) and Martin Lorentzon (co-founder, director, ~9,8% of the capital / ~41,6% of the voting rights) - together ~24,1% of the capital but ~70,7% of the voting rights combined. Governance transition agreed on 30/09/2025 and effective 1 January 2026: Ek hands the CEO role to Gustav Soderstrom and Alex Norstrom (co-CEOs since 2023 as co-presidents), becomes Executive Chairman focused on strategy/capital allocation/regulatory, while retaining voting control.

items.title: Several plaintiffs' law firms (Schall Law Firm, Pomerantz LLP, Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman) have opened securities fraud investigations, following the roughly 12,4% fall in the stock on 28 April 2026 after the Q1 2026 results release: Q2 Premium subscriber guidance (299M) below consensus (300,3M) and weaker-than-expected Q1 advertising revenue.
items.allegedBy: Plaintiffs' law firms (Schall Law Firm, Pomerantz LLP, Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman LLC, among others)
items.source: GlobeNewswire/PRNewswire/AccessNewswire press releases from the firms (May-June 2026); no formally filed complaint found as at the date of this refresh

compliance.note: A single solicitation episode identified (Q1 26, tied to the Q2 guidance), still at the preliminary investigation stage. The MLC (Mechanical Licensing Collective) litigation on the calculation of US mechanical royalties is NOT covered here: it is a regulatory/contractual interpretation dispute over the applicable royalty rate, not a fraud allegation - tracked in hypothese.text (EVENTS section) in line with the strict scope of this field.

clesRetenues: Q Reif Ehrlich (most promising products over 3-5 years) - Gustav Soderstrom cites first and foremost Reserved (ticketing, already perceived as one of the best features ever launched), the large taste model (LTM, scaling laws holding up internally), Song DNA (100M+ users) and music videos (boost to discovery of new tracks); longer term, Remix/Covers and Talk to Spotify.

Q Reif Ehrlich (advertising growth, programmatic momentum) - Alex Norstrom confirms the near-complete migration (~99% of impressions) to the proprietary ad stack, automated channels at ~40% of ad revenue (vs 30% in Q1), 33 000 active advertisers (+60% YoY); Christian Luiga specifies that the advertising margin should converge from ~20% today towards ~40% over time as self-serve scales up (consistent with the Investor Day).

Q Greenfield (why so few labels signed for generative AI music) - Alex Norstrom announces an agreement with Merlin (30 000 independent labels) on top of the UMG agreement from May, a '3 C' framework (consent, credit, compensation); Gustav Soderstrom specifies that a complete catalogue is not necessary in order to launch, a research preview will precede the full launch to gather preference data via reinforcement learning.

Q Patterson (costs/benefits of open source vs Claude and other proprietary models) - Gustav Soderstrom explains that the large taste model is built by continued pre-training on open source models, and that the internal tool 'Chirp' makes it possible to switch between paid models and self-hosted open source ones depending on the best price/performance ratio, soon to be offered to other companies.

Q Levi/Black (slowdown in the Q3 MAU guidance, competitive environment) - Alex Norstrom and Gustav Soderstrom confirm a deliberate choice to 'pull the monetisation lever rather than the growth lever' in certain emerging markets (India, Indonesia) - added friction on the free tier, deprecation of low-end Android support - management states explicitly that this should NOT affect subscriber growth in the near term, a curve already observed in Latin America in the past.

Q Greenfield (Reserved traction) - Alex Norstrom indicates roughly 100 000 tickets reserved since the US launch in June with Live Nation, several tours having sold through 100% of the allocation, which led Live Nation to increase it mid-tour; still very early, limited to the United States for now.

Q Bazinet (are agreements with all the major labels needed before launching music AI) - Gustav Soderstrom answers no, a complete catalogue is never necessary (as at Spotify's creation), the research preview will precede the full launch decision.

Q Sheridan (monetisation potential beyond 300M subscribers) - Alex Norstrom points to plausible eventual global penetration of around 15% (vs ~4% currently), with priority given to raising the value/price ratio via add-on modules (covers/remixes, Personal Podcasts, Audiobooks+) rather than simple price increases.

Q Patterson (time spent vs Netflix, 211 Md hours vs 191 Md) - Alex Norstrom stresses that Spotify engagement covers far more contexts/devices (speakers, car, gaming, sleep, study) than screen-based services; the key internal metric is the number of 'active days', up again this quarter, judged the most correlated with customer lifetime value.

Q Madhavan (metrics for the AI products - listening hours, conversion, churn) - Gustav Soderstrom indicates that the AI experiences now reach ~25% of active users, Prompted Playlist already adopted by 14M of the first 100M targeted users, and that the LTM measurably improves 'active days' (the hardest metric to move).

Q Anmuth (implied acceleration in operating costs in Q3) - Christian Luiga confirms that the ~200 M€ increase in annual OpEx (marketing + AI, no headcount) remains fully under control and was already announced, Q3 cost growth expected broadly stable vs Q2 excluding FX/social charges, moderation still expected in Q4; Gustav Soderstrom adds that these costs (compute + marketing) are entirely reversible, unlike a multi-year CapEx.

Q Anmuth (timing of the add-on modules, ARPU impact in H2/2027) - Alex Norstrom gives no precise timing or ARPU guidance, cites Audiobooks+ (ARR doubled since launch) as an example of a 'structural' ARPU increase distinct from a simple price increase.

Q Helfstein (read-across from the July Apple Music price increase) - Alex Norstrom does not comment on a competitor's pricing policy but sees in it a validation of the sector's willingness to pay; Spotify positions itself as the price leader of the category.

Q Bazinet (sector-wide slowdown in premium subscriber growth according to the record labels, long-term confidence) - Alex Norstrom says he is very confident, gives no quantified long-term guidance, but reaffirms optimising for a 'healthy funnel' rather than an isolated growth target.

engagementsStructurants.engagement: 2030 financial targets presented at the Investor Day of 21/05/2026: mid-teens revenue CAGR, gross margin 35-40%, operating margin >20%, strong FCF growth; symbolic milestones of 1 Md subscribers and 100 Md$ of revenue reaffirmed.
Research preview of the AI-generated music remix/covers product (already backed by the UMG and Merlin agreements) announced as the next step before a full launch, with no precise date communicated.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 26: revenue ~EUR 5.0bn (+14% YoY, ARPU consistent with Q2, improving ad growth still expected to inflect toward double digits in H2 26); gross margin 32.9% (+130bp YoY, includes new-product reinvestment and the recurring Q3 regulatory-fee charge in one market); operating income EUR 670M with temporarily elevated opex (Q3 opex growth roughly consistent with Q2 ex-FX and social charges); MAU 788M (+11M, deliberately dampened by the emerging-markets monetization pivot, developed-markets growth stable); Premium subscribers 305M (+5M net, no near-term subscriber impact expected from the free-tier friction).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No formal full-year numeric guidance (Spotify guides one quarter ahead), but management reiterated - unchanged vs Q1 and the May Investor Day - that both gross margin and operating margin improve for full-year 2026 despite ~EUR 200M of incremental marketing/AI opex concentrated in Q2-Q3 (compute and marketing only, headcount flat, framed as fully controllable and reversible), with a moderation in year-over-year opex growth in Q4; meaningful year-over-year FCF growth in 2026 reconfirmed; ads business still expected to inflect toward double-digit growth in H2 26; 2030 Investor Day targets (mid-teens revenue CAGR, 35-40% gross margin, >20% operating margin, strong FCF growth) reaffirmed.
pointsCles: 300M Premium subscribers crossed for the first time (+7M net, 1M above guidance, growth across all regions); MAU 777M (+12% YoY, +16M net but 1M below forecast); revenue EUR 4.8bn, +15% YoY constant currency accelerating from +14% in Q1 (Premium +16% cc on subs +9% and ARPU +7.4%; ads +3% cc with automated channels at ~40% of ad revenue vs ~30% in Q1 and 33,000 active advertisers, +60% YoY).

Record gross margin 33.4% (+193bp YoY, 30bp above guidance, helped by a one-time Canadian digital-services-tax accrual reversal); operating income EUR 655M, EUR 25M above the 630M guide (EUR 16M ex favorable social charges), 13.7% operating margin; diluted EPS EUR 2.61 ($3.01) below consensus - the miss sits below the operating line, not in the core business; FCF EUR 797M (+14% YoY); EUR 9.4bn cash, no debt beyond leases; $662M buybacks YTD through Aug 3 (+30% vs 2025 pace, ~1% of shares retired since the 2025 restart) and management now expects recurring cash returns even alongside M&A.

Deliberate emerging-markets monetization pivot: added friction in the free tier (ad load, feature limits), sign-up screening and low-end Android deprecation in markets like India/Indonesia will dent Q3 MAU (guided 788M, +11M) but management explicitly expects no near-term impact on subscriber growth (Q3 guided 305M, +5M), replaying the LatAm free-to-paid conversion curve.

Monetization stack thickens beyond price rises: Audiobooks+ passed $100M ARR and has doubled since last disclosure in only a few markets; Reserved (Live Nation, US-only) booked ~100,000 tickets with sold-out allocations upsized mid-tour; AI products reach ~25% of actives (Prompted Playlists 14M of first 100M users, Large Taste Model measurably lifting active days); Merlin deal (30,000 indie labels) joins UMG for consented AI covers/remixes with a public research preview as next step; internal AI tooling (Honk/Chirp) keeps headcount flat for a third year with revenue per employee on track to double.

hypothese.summary: Global leader in audio streaming, crosses 300M Premium subscribers in Q2 26 with a record gross margin (33,4%). Q2 is presented by the market as a 'miss' (EPS 2,61€ vs consensus 2,76€) but the operating line itself beats guidance (OI +25 M€ above) - the gap comes from items below the operating line. The 2030 Investor Day targets from May (mid-teens revenue CAGR, operating margin >20%) are now the reference framework for the thesis, reaffirmed without revision this quarter.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Spotify runs in a structural-profitability regime since 2024 and confirmed it at Q2 26 with a symbolic milestone: 300M Premium subscribers, record 33.4% gross margin, revenue +15% cc accelerating (vs +14% Q1). The March-2026 full redemption of the Exchangeable Notes cleaned the EBIT-to-net bridge (no more FVTPL noise). Full-year margin improvement is guided DESPITE a ~200M marketing/AI surcost concentrated in Q2-Q3.

== THESIS READ ==
- Pricing power + tier architecture (Music Pro upsell) is the margin engine; the 300M base makes each ARPU move material. Watch: Music Pro adoption and churn response to price moves.
- The AI/marketing surcost is framed as offensive spend with Q4 moderation promised. Watch: Q4 opex moderation actually landing.
- Net cash compounds fast (7.5 -> 19.5bn by 2030) with financial income becoming a real EPS line (~3.5% yield modeled, clean post-redemption). Watch: capital-return policy emergence - none exists yet.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
IFRS base, no aggressive management adjustments. ETR ~23% (H1 observed 23.1-24.3%). Net share dilution ~+1%/yr (SBC exceeds accelerated buybacks). Omnium 2026 deliberately below street (surcost absorption). FY25 financial line carried Exchangeable-Notes FVTPL volatility - documented in the bridge, gone from 2026.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 19.6bn (+14%), EBIT 2,835M (14.5%), EPS 12.13; 2027-2030: revenue +15-16%/yr, EBIT margin to 20.5%, conversion ~1x boosted by financial income. Watch: gross-margin trajectory vs the 33.4% record; label negotiations cycle; video/audiobook mix economics.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Nov); Q4 opex moderation proof; Music Pro tier rollout; 2027 margin framing.

ancrages.moteur: Revenue growth anchored on the Investor Day 2030 framework (mid-teens revenue CAGR), confirmed by the acceleration observed in H1 26 (+14% Q1 -> +15% Q2 on a constant currency basis) - ARPU (pricing + audiobooks/add-ons mix) and MAU/subscriber growth in declining double digits over the projection horizon.

Operating margin expansion anchored on the Investor Day 2030 target (>20%, high-end target 20-22% per sell-side readings), starting from a 2026 margin depressed by the ~200 M€ of extra marketing/AI cost now officially quantified and confirmed (concentrated in Q2-Q3, moderation agreed for Q4 26/2027).

Net financial income ~3,5% on a growing net cash position (9,4 Md€ at 30/06/26, no debt other than lease obligations), now entirely post-repayment of the Exchangeable Notes (March 2026) - no fair value volatility left from the convertible debt, movements in the TME stake excluded (pure optionality).
Normative ETR 23%, confirmed by the effective rates actually observed in Q1 26 (23,1%) and Q2 26 (24,3%) - no one-off tax credit identified this half, unlike Q4 2025.
Net dilution ~1%/yr (SBC above buybacks despite a buyback pace accelerated by 30% vs 2025 - 662 M$ repurchased as at 3 August, ~1% of shares outstanding since the programme resumed in 2025).

2026 extra marketing/AI cost now officially quantified by management at ~200 M€, concentrated in Q2-Q3 26, with moderation explicitly agreed for Q4 26 and 2027 - treated as a temporary drag on the 2026 operating margin only, not a recurring structural charge.
